messages:
ashley: Heads up — customers reporting degraded responses from hosted inference in eu-west-3, error stream shows timeout + occasional 503s.
omar: I'm seeing a surge in request queue length on the eu-west-3 serving tier starting ~08:34 UTC. Could be a batching regression.
kai: Any recent deploys to that pool?
omar: small config push to dynamic-batching yesterday. rolling back is an option.
oncall-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-5555 created and assigned to infra-oncall. https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-5555
ashley: For immediate mitigation: enable real-time fallback routing to reduce batching on the pool. I'll flip the flag.
ashley: Command: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/flags -d '{"flag":"realtime_fallback.eu-west-3","value":true}'
omar: Applied. Traffic shifted — requests hitting fallback path are ~47% now. Queue length dropping.
kai: Noted a correlated increase in cold-start latency in the fallback path; keeping it enabled while we stabilize.
cs-ops: CS notified affected enterprise customers and opened a support case list. Sending templated message now.
status-bot: Status page updated: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/PD-5555 - "Degraded responses in EU-WEST-3. Mitigation: routing to real-time fallback."
omar: Rolling back dynamic-batching config on eu-west-3 to previous revision. kubectl rollout undo deployment/batcher -n prod --to-revision=12
oncall-bot: Rollback job started by omar.
omar: Rollback completed. batcher pods back to stable image. Queue lengths normalized.
ashley: Error rate down to baseline. Keeping fallback routing for 15 more minutes to warm caches, then we'll revert flag.
kai: Follow-ups: 1) add regression test for dynamic-batching under skewed arrival patterns 2) add canary to config pushes for batcher 3) improve alerting threshold to catch queue-length anomalies earlier.
omar: Filing tickets: INF-8001, INF-8002, INF-8003
ashley: Incident set to monitoring. Postmortem draft ETA 4h, will include timeline and customer list.
oncall-bot: Incident PD-5555 status: mitigated -> monitoring
